restrictions: ONE BROWSER, ONE MACHINE, ONE DAY: Chrome 157.0.8103.51 (stable, installed by the owner) on the physical Windows 11 Pro 26H2 x64 laptop of validation/platforms/windows-11-x64.json, runs of 2026-11-15, one run set of the 15 vectors and one series of 10 default runs. Under the PoC rule (owner decision 2026-11-15) this one current browser stands for the Modern Web UI; no other Chrome version, Edge, Firefox or Safari, and no other operating system or machine (Chrome on Android, macOS or Linux) was run. Firefox and Safari (recent) are not required by the owner and were not tried.

HEADLESS, LOOPBACK: Chrome was run with --headless=new --disable-gpu, a new throw-away --user-data-dir per run (under the system temp folder, deleted afterwards; the owner's profile was never opened), no extension, component update or sync. The page was loaded over HTTP from 127.0.0.1 (a Python server of tools/run_vectors.py, loomora.wasm sent as application/wasm so that WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming was used), not from file://, not over HTTPS or the Internet, and no headed window was opened: GPU rendering, window chrome, focus behaviour of a visible tab and the ArrayBuffer fallback of native.ts (a server that does not send application/wasm) were not exercised.

THE PROBE RUNS WERE READ FROM A DUMPED DOM: each vector started a new chrome.exe with --dump-dom --virtual-time-budget=15000 and the record was read from <pre id="probe"> (title LOOMORA_PROBE_DONE). Under --virtual-time-budget the page clock (Date.now) is virtual, so display_ms (74 to 110 ms for the 15 vectors, 77 to 237 ms for the 10 default runs) is the page's own figure on that clock and is not a wall-clock measurement; the wall clock of chrome.exe from its start to its exit is 0.9 to 1.2 s (a cold start with a new profile: process start, page load, WebAssembly compile, DOM dump and exit). Without virtual time (the DevTools run, typing-check-log.txt) the default greeting appeared 820 ms after Page.navigate in the stored run (an earlier run of the same script, not stored, showed 352 ms). All are far below the 3,000 ms of SC-001.

TYPING: 'Marie' was typed with Input.dispatchKeyEvent of the DevTools protocol (a key down with text and a key up per character, into the focused textarea whose content was selected): real key events for the page, but sent by a script, not a person, not a physical keyboard, no IME, no dead keys, no clipboard paste, no touch keyboard. The 1,000-character limit was exercised only through the probe input (the two vectors of more than 1,000 UTF-16 units were cut to 1,000), not by typing 1,001 characters or by pasting.

THEMES: the light and the dark palettes were looked at (one screenshot each) and read from the computed styles with prefers-color-scheme emulated through the DevTools protocol (greeting on card 18.11:1 light, 14.80:1 dark; field text 16.75:1 and 16.43:1). In headless Chrome 157 only --force-dark-mode switched the scheme on the command line; --blink-settings=preferredColorScheme=1 had no effect (see screenshots-log.txt). The Windows dark-theme setting of the machine was not changed, and forced colours (Windows high contrast), zoom, DPI above 100% and text scaling were not tried.

peak_rss_kb is performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize in KiB (886 to 906) read by the page: the JavaScript heap in use at the end of the start, not the peak and not the memory of the browser processes (the Windows 11 native UI reports 112,696 to 112,952 KiB of the whole process: the figures are not comparable). The end-of-life banner was never shown (the Web family is never end of life for the backend, eol_warning_shown false in every record), so its look and contrast in a browser were not checked.

NOT RUN: a failed start (wasm blocked, a very old browser), a slow network, repeated loads in one profile (every run had a cold, empty profile and the browser cache was bypassed by Cache-Control: no-store), concurrent tabs, memory pressure, and the 15 vectors a second time. Process hygiene was checked for every run: no chrome.exe whose command line names the run's profile folder was left after any run (0 in all 15 runs, 10 default runs and the DevTools run); only processes started by these runs were counted and terminated.
